claims.statement: agent/dashboard/options.py is the single registry of selectable models: SUPPORTED_MODELS is a hand-maintained list of ModelOption records (provider-prefixed id, label, per-model efforts list, default_effort, supports_images), and SUPPORTED_MODEL_IDS is the frozen set every resolution layer checks membership against.

Deprecated model ids are not canonically replaced: DEPRECATED_MODEL_REPLACEMENTS has empty values and canonical_model_pair always returns None. Deprecated ids are excluded from provider_fallback_pair and defer to defaults, while unsupported non-deprecated ids may use same-provider and, where possible, same-Claude-family fallback.

default_model_pair() is the deployment-level terminal fallback: it reads LLM_MODEL_ID and LLM_REASONING_EFFORT, validates that the resulting model is supported and default-eligible, and raises ValueError for an unsupported model or effort.

For a hosted agent run, the factory seeds workspace main/subagent defaults, applies a profile only when no stored thread model exists, then uses stored thread settings when present; a valid explicit configurable agent_model_id/agent_effort replaces that snapshot and the resolved settings are persisted back to the thread.

Every workspace-default resolution routes candidates through _resolve_default_pair, which returns the pair if supported, else the same-provider fallback, else the global default, guaranteeing a valid constructible pair even when persisted settings are stale or unknown.

Effective workspace settings overlay sparse workspace overrides over the instance record keyed 'default' in the ['team_settings'] namespace and hardcoded defaults; get_workspace_settings fails soft to hardcoded defaults if its store reads fail.

Per-user profiles live in the ['profiles'] namespace holding main and optional subagent pairs, repository/branch and PR preferences, direct-message and routing preferences; profile-editable settings are deliberately split from encrypted GitHub OAuth tokens in ['oauth_tokens'] so concurrent saves cannot clobber each other.

provider_model_kwargs translates a resolved effort string into provider-specific kwargs by dispatching on the model id prefix: OpenAI gets a reasoning dict, Anthropic gets adaptive/summarized thinking plus an effort field, Gemini 3+ gets thinking_level, Fireworks gets model_kwargs.reasoning_effort, and Baseten gets reasoning_effort for low/high/max.

Fable models are gated workspace-wide: disabling Fable rewrites submitted defaults to a safe non-Fable Anthropic model, hides Fable from the workspace options response, and the factory gates main, subagent, and title models after snapshot resolution so disabled Fable is not constructed.

Per-repo custom instructions are records stored in the ['agent_instructions'] namespace keyed by owner/name; the run factory resolves them on an initial thread and freezes them into thread settings, while construct_system_prompt renders them as 'Repository-specific Custom Instructions' for the shared thread prompt.

Per-user instructions are attached to the triggering user's message via construct_sender_context and explicitly scoped to only the current turn, distinct from repository instructions embedded in the shared system prompt.

Adaptive model routing is resolved from a profile preference over the workspace setting, then frozen in thread settings; dashboard auto/explicit selection can override it, and ModelSelectionMiddleware classifies the latest human task with balanced fallback while forcing performance in plan mode.

Skills are mounted as read-only bundled, organization, and where credential scope permits user sources for hosted runs, while desktop uses state-backed user skills; WorkspaceSkillsMiddleware filters metadata to its own sources and user and organization skill mutation have distinct authorization boundaries.
Instruction authority is AGENTS.md over repository custom instructions, with repository custom instructions over workspace and sender-level user instructions.
